key_insight: MANTRA is testing whether early angiotensin-II, instead of norepinephrine, can better correct sepsis-related RAAS dysfunction and reshape immune responses in septic shock.
clinical_relevance: If successful, the trial could support a more mechanism-guided vasopressor strategy for septic shock patients with RAAS dysregulation.
method: Multicenter, open-label, randomized 1:1 trial in adults with septic shock on norepinephrine-equivalent dose 0.10–0.50 mcg/kg/min.
Compare primary angiotensin-II vs norepinephrine over 48 hours, with angiotensin-II titrated up to 40 ng/kg/min and norepinephrine up to 35 mcg/min.
Primary endpoint: change in plasma renin from baseline to 24 hours using a linear mixed-effects model; secondary endpoints include vasopressor burden, organ-support–free days, and safety events.
evidence_signal: The protocol is powered at 90% to detect a 25% between-group difference in 24-hour renin, with serial biomarker and clinical outcome assessment over 28 days.
watch_item: Because this is an open-label mechanistic trial in a narrow shock-dose window, results may be influenced by crossover, protocol discontinuation, and limited generalizability.
paper_title: Mechanistic Assessment of Norepinephrine Therapy versus Angiotensin-II in Septic Shock (MANTRA): Study Protocol for a multicenter randomized trial
